newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woman thought buried in Thredbo turns up alive.
newsitem.headline: Woman thought buried in Thredbo turns up alive.

text.p: A woman assumed to have been buried in a landslide at an Australia ski village has turned up alive and well, police said on Monday.
The woman, assumed for the past five days to have been swept away by the landslide at Thredbo village on Wednesday night, was never in danger, a police spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The woman reported to have been swept away by the landslide while walking past the lodges with her husband is safe and well," the police spokeswoman said.
She was staying in a ski lodge near the landslide and rushed with her husband to the scene late on Wednesday night to help with rescue efforts, but the pair became separated, police said.
The couple eventually found each other, but only after the husband had reported her missing to rescuers.

"Rescuers assumed she must be missing. Apparently when the couple reunited, both in a state of distress, they packed up their belongings and returned to their country home," the police spokeswoman said.
Police declined to identify the couple. The woman did not come forward earlier because she thought media reports of her disappearance referred to someone else.
The news means that 19 people were buried in the landslide, not 20 as previously thought.
One survivor, ski instructor Stuart Diver, 27, was rescued from the rubble on Saturday night after surviving in a concrete tomb for 65 hours.
Nine bodies have been removed from the site, leaving nine people still missing.
